title: Pressure Building Behind the Scenes

patient.name: Mr Daniel Tan Wei Jie
patient.presenting_complaint: Referred for Cirrus OCT optic disc / RNFL scan — raised eye pressure with a family history of glaucoma

history.hpc: Mr Tan tells you 'My vision a bit blur for the past few months lah, especially the left side.' He came in worried after a screening found his eye pressure was high. He has no eye pain, no redness, and no headache. The doctor reviewed him, noted the raised pressures, and ordered a Cirrus OCT scan of the optic nerve and retinal nerve fibre layer in both eyes before the next clinic review.
history.pmhx: No medical history. Short-sighted, wears glasses. No previous eye surgery or eye injury.
history.family_hx: Grandmother had glaucoma and went blind in one eye in old age
history.social_hx: Full-time student. Non-smoker. Long hours on the computer.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Clear cornea, deep anterior chambers, no anterior segment abnormality (NAD)
examination_findings.fundus: Doctor notes mildly enlarged cup-to-disc ratio bilaterally, suspicious for early glaucomatous change

cirrus_oct_optic_disc.result: Borderline average RNFL thickness with inferior quadrant thinning in the left eye; symmetry and disc parameters flagged for doctor review

diagnosis: Cirrus OCT optic disc and RNFL scan completed bilaterally with good signal strength. Findings show borderline RNFL thinning, more marked inferiorly in the left eye, alongside raised intraocular pressures and a positive family history. Findings reported to the doctor as a glaucoma suspect for correlation and possible visual field testing — no independent diagnosis made by the technician.

immediate: Confirm patient identity (full name and a second identifier) and confirm both eyes are to be scanned
Explain the procedure: non-contact, patient sits at the machine and looks at a fixation target, takes a few minutes per eye
Enter patient details accurately and select the Optic Disc Cube 200x200 protocol as ordered
Position patient at the chinrest with forehead against the rest and align the optic disc within the scan window
Ensure the optic disc is centred and focused before capture; ask the patient to keep the eye open and fixate steadily
Check signal strength (aim 6/10 or higher) and repeat any scan with poor signal, blinks, or motion artefact
Print/export the RNFL thickness map, ONH analysis and symmetry report for the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to correlate OCT RNFL findings with IOP, optic disc appearance and any visual field results
Patient may be booked for Humphrey visual field testing and repeat IOP/pachymetry
Baseline OCT to be repeated at intervals to monitor for progression if glaucoma is confirmed
patient_education: Explain the scan measures the thickness of the nerve layer at the back of the eye, which can be affected by high eye pressure
Reassure the patient the test is quick, painless and does not touch the eye
Advise the patient that raised eye pressure often has no symptoms, so attending follow-up and any field tests is important

key_points: Confirms patient identity and confirms both eyes are to be scanned
Elicits the relevant risk factors: raised IOP and family history of glaucoma
Confirms which scan the doctor ordered (optic disc / RNFL, not macular)
Explains the non-contact nature of the OCT procedure to the patient
Selects the Optic Disc Cube 200x200 protocol and enters patient details accurately
Centres and focuses on the optic disc and obtains steady fixation
Checks signal strength and repeats scans with poor signal or motion artefact
Captures both eyes and records RNFL average, quadrant values and cup-to-disc ratio
Recognises that borderline/reduced RNFL with raised IOP raises suspicion of glaucoma
Understands the purpose of the RNFL/ONH scan in glaucoma assessment
Does not diagnose glaucoma independently — reports findings to the doctor
Notes the inter-eye asymmetry and inferior thinning as findings to highlight
Produces good-quality scans (adequate signal strength, no motion artefact) for both eyes
Hands the RNFL and ONH report promptly to the doctor
Educates the patient that raised eye pressure is often symptomless and follow-up matters
Documents IOP and scan quality accurately
